basis: Skeletal dysplasia, immunodeficiency and neurodevelopmental impairment define the syndrome; developmental delay in 6/6 and SCID in 7/12.
Congenital muscular dystrophy with defining brain and eye malformations; retinal dysplasia, cataract and optic atrophy are documented.
Purine metabolism disorder; nephropathy, intellectual disability and dystonia annotated at 30-79%. Neurologic severity varies; gout and stones are occasional.
Psychiatric disorder of sexual preference without defining damage to an organ axis.
Pathologic vascularization of the cornea; local vessel growth does not establish systemic cardiovascular disease.
Lymphoid-cell malignancy arising in the pharyngeal tonsil; lymphoma warrants the immune axis. Pharyngeal location maps to pulmonary.
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 20/21; direct skeletal myopathy with fatty replacement in 2/2 assessed, although muscle sampling is very limited.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; respiratory insufficiency in 21/21 is due to muscle weakness, without intrinsic lung damage. Ophthalmoplegia is 6/21.
Carcinoma arising in the esophagus; salivary gland type describes histology.
Cerebellar degeneration and ataxia; nystagmus, dysphagia and urinary incontinence reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than separate organ damage.
Neoplasm originating in or occupying the duodenum.
Defining lymphatic vascular dysfunction causes lymphedema in 5/7; posterior nasal airway atresia occurs in 7/7.
Compression neuropathy of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve; sensory symptoms do not indicate skin damage.
Familial cerebral EEG pattern; neurologic classification reflects the defining finding, although this pattern can be a benign variant.
Joubert brain malformation and developmental impairment; retinal dysfunction suggested by abnormal electroretinogram in 1/3, at the threshold with limited data.
Acute exacerbation of immune-mediated inflammatory airway disease with bronchoconstriction, mucus plugging and airway edema.
Central and peripheral neurologic dysfunction defines the disorder; respiratory distress and infections do not establish direct pulmonary damage.
Complement-mediated hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury define aHUS; direct microvascular endothelial injury and thrombosis are defining pathology.
Autoimmune destruction of adrenal cortex; pigmentation, hypotension, gastrointestinal symptoms and salt wasting do not establish direct extra-adrenal organ damage.
Central movement disorder with dystonia and parkinsonism; swallowing and laryngeal manifestations arise from abnormal motor control.
Skeletal anomalies, congenital heart disease and intellectual disability define syndrome; cleft lip/palate is a major defining oral defect. Hypogonadism omitted under cap.
Defining microstomia/palatal, external-ear and eyelid anomalies; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%. Skin and hair findings are predominantly morphology without established damage.
Bone fragility defines OI16; tooth agenesis and prolonged bleeding time each reported in 1/1 assessed. Hearing loss lacks frequency evidence; blue sclerae are non-damaging.
Familial infantile epilepsy; tonic-clonic and focal seizures are defining neurologic manifestations.
Atrophy of tongue papillae affects oral mucosa; no specific infectious or autoimmune mechanism is established.
